title: Sourdough starter: pages kept as regenerable seed-plus-recipe stubs
idea: Forced connection: a baker keeps a pinch of starter, not the bread. Add an MMU/OS page class 'regenerable' whose PTE points to a 64-byte recipe (PRNG seed, generator kernel ID, parameters); on fault a near-memory engine re-materialises the 4 KB page in ~1 us and under pressure the page is simply dropped instead of swapped. Targets init weights, RoPE/sin tables, lookup tables, decompressed assets, pattern pages and deterministic intermediates.
why: Cost per bit / capacity: 5-25% of resident footprint in AI and HPC jobs is derivable; dropping instead of storing it gives 1.05-1.3x effective capacity with no new DRAM.

title: Tetris: memory-controller line compaction collapses fragmented heaps
idea: Like Tetris rows clearing once full, a controller-side engine migrates live 64 B lines out of sparsely occupied pages into dense pages during idle cycles, tracked by an SRAM-cached line-remap table so software pointers never change; fully emptied pages are handed back to the OS.
why: Allocator fragmentation strands 15-40% of heap DRAM in long-running services and Python/AI runtimes; reclaiming half of it is ~1.1-1.25x capacity.

title: Airline overbooking: sell 140% of rack DRAM, keep CXL standby seats
idea: Treat DRAM like airline seats: provision each server at ~70% of its tenants' summed peak, size a rack-level CXL pool from no-show statistics, and 'bump' the lowest-value pages (compress first, then pool) when a peak lands; the hypervisor publishes a per-VM bump-probability SLA.
why: Fleets provisioned for sum-of-peaks leave 25-40% of DRAM idle; overbooking math cuts DIMMs purchased 20-30% at a quantified SLA risk.

title: Interlibrary loan: one shared weight copy serving sixteen hosts
idea: Like libraries lending one rare book, place a single read-only copy of popular model weights behind a CXL 3 switch, mapped read-only into 8-16 inference hosts that each keep only a hot-layer cache; an epoch counter replaces coherence traffic because the data is immutable.
why: Inference farms replicate the same 100-800 GB of weights per host; sharing cuts weight DRAM 8-16x per pod at +100-200 ns access hidden by layer prefetch.

title: Zipper merge: approximate cross-request KV block deduplication
idea: Two lanes zip into one: hash every 16-token KV block with locality-sensitive hashing; when a new block lies within epsilon of a canonical block from any request (same RAG passage at a different offset, near-identical prompts), store a pointer plus a sparse int4 residual, applying a RoPE offset correction at read.
why: Exact prefix sharing misses non-prefix repeats; in RAG/agent fleets 30-70% of KV is near-duplicate, giving 2-4x KV capacity relief.

title: Ant pheromone trails: refresh operations decay per-page hotness counters
idea: Ant trails fade unless re-walked: keep a 3-bit hotness counter per page in spare on-die ECC/metadata bits; accesses increment it and the DRAM's own refresh, which already opens every row, decrements it for free, giving the controller hardware-aged heat maps to drive tiering with zero sampling overhead.
why: Tiering accuracy limits how much DRAM cheaper tiers can replace; free precise hotness lets 30-50% of footprint leave DRAM versus ~15-20% with page-table scanning.

title: Origami: address unit stores structured matrices as their generators
idea: Fold rather than cut more paper: an address-transform unit in the memory controller treats tagged regions as symmetric, Toeplitz, circulant, banded or block-repeated, storing only the generating vector or triangle and computing (i,j) to generator offset on every access, so software still sees a dense matrix.
why: n^2 to n (or 2x for symmetric) storage for covariance, Hessian, convolution, positional-bias and kernel matrices in HPC and science codes, with no code rewrite.

title: Bus timetable: compiled exact page-in schedule for model inference
idea: Inference access order is as fixed as a bus timetable: the compiler emits a cycle-accurate schedule of which weight/KV pages must arrive when, and a DMA engine streams them from flash or CXL into a DRAM ring sized for ~2 layers plus slack, with no demand paging at all.
why: Batch/offline inference needs only the in-flight window resident; DRAM per model drops 10-50x when flash bandwidth covers per-layer compute time.

title: Pawn shop: internal market where idle gigabytes are pledged
idea: Tenants pawn idle memory: a broker daemon pays credits for GB released through a balloon driver, guarantees redemption within 50 ms from a compressed/CXL reserve, and clears prices by auction every minute so memory flows to the highest-value job.
why: Prices reveal and recover idle allocations (often 30-50%); 15-25% fewer DIMMs per fleet and a direct lever during the 4x price spike.

title: Ice-cube tray: compressed lines carry size class inside freed ECC
idea: Each ice-tray slot has a fixed shape: compress every 64 B line into one of four slot classes, and when a line shrinks by at least 4 B write its 2-bit class and slot pointer into the freed bits alongside stronger ECC, so the controller never fetches a separate metadata table; incompressible lines use standard ECC with a flag symbol.
why: Metadata misses (10-30% latency penalty) are what kill hardware memory compression; embedding metadata makes 1.5-2x line compression viable at near-zero latency cost.

title: Bicycle gears: bit-plane tiering serves weights at shiftable precision
idea: Store weights transposed into bit-planes: the 4 most-significant planes stay in DRAM/HBM, low planes live in CXL or flash; each request 'shifts gear' by fetching only as many planes as its quality tier needs, and speculative decoding uses MSB-only planes as a free draft model.
why: Cuts DRAM held for weights 2-4x without storing multiple quantized copies; fetch energy scales with precision actually used.

title: Hourglass: retention-failed dies hold only millisecond-lived data
idea: Sand runs out on a known schedule: bin dies that fail 64 ms retention (normally scrapped or downbinned) into 'hourglass DIMMs' with refresh disabled, and let the allocator place only data with guaranteed lifetimes under 5 ms there (activations, pipeline and staging buffers) via a lifetime tag in the allocation API.
why: Recovers several percent of wafer output lost to retention fallout and removes refresh energy (fact 3) for that data; supply gain at zero fab capex.

title: Kaleidoscope: one tensor copy, many layouts via controller remapping
idea: A kaleidoscope shows many patterns from one set of beads: the memory controller exposes row-major, column-major and tiled 'views' of a single physical tensor through programmable address swizzles, so training no longer keeps transposed weight copies, layout-converted buffers or im2col expansions.
why: Duplicate layouts and expansions take 10-30% of training memory; removing them is 1.1-1.4x capacity.

title: Morse code: Huffman exponents decoded at line rate in controller
idea: Morse gives E a single dot: entropy-code only the exponent field of BF16/FP8 tensors per 4 KB block (about 2.5-3 bits of information in 8) and decode in a 16-lane table-driven unit in the memory controller, keeping sign and mantissa raw for fixed-latency random access.
why: Lossless ~25-30% capacity reduction on all floating-point weights and activations.

title: Bonsai pruning: memory-side unit trims never-attended KV tokens
idea: Prune what never sees light: the accelerator streams per-token attention-mass sums to a small memory-side 'bonsai' unit that keeps exponentially decayed importance per KV block and evicts or downgrades blocks below threshold in the background, off the decode critical path.
why: Most long-context tokens get negligible attention; 3-8x KV reduction at small quality loss with zero decode stall.

title: Vending machine: bill memory per compressed resident byte-second
idea: Pay for what drops out of the machine: cloud providers meter memory by actual resident bytes after compression and dedup, sampled each second, instead of allocated GB, plus a discounted 'evictable' class; every developer gains a direct reward for compressing, freeing and sharing.
why: Shifts incentives fleet-wide; a 10-20% footprint cut across cloud demand equals several fabs of output during the shortage.

title: Shipping container: universal compressed-page format across all tiers
idea: Like the ISO container ending break-bulk cargo, standardize a 4 KB compressed-page envelope (codec ID, dictionary hash, size class, checksum) that CPUs, GPUs, CXL memory, NICs and SSDs read and write natively, so pages move between tiers and machines without decompress/recompress.
why: Recompression cost keeps compressed tiers small; a standard lets 30-50% of footprint stay compressed end-to-end (1.3-1.8x capacity).

title: Chameleon skin: lines change encoding instead of location
idea: A chameleon changes colour, not position: rather than migrating cold pages to another device, the controller re-encodes them in place (raw, then light base-delta, then heavy dictionary/entropy) as they cool and returns the slack to a common pool; hot accesses promote them back to raw.
why: Delivers tiering's capacity benefit without a second memory device or link; 1.3-2x effective capacity in the same DIMMs.

title: Telephone switchboard: optical circuit switch re-patches memory sleds
idea: An operator plugging cords: a MEMS optical circuit switch at rack level connects any socket's CXL links to any memory sled, re-patched every few minutes by a scheduler, so stranded memory on one server becomes another's without packet-switch latency or buffering.
why: About 25% of datacenter DRAM is stranded; circuit-switched pooling recovers most of it at near direct-attach latency.

title: Dictionary: fleet-trained compression dictionaries pinned per workload
idea: Train zstd-style dictionaries per workload class (JVM heaps, Python objects, embeddings) from fleet samples, ship them signed with the binary, and pin them in the hardware compressor's SRAM so even single 4 KB pages compress against a rich shared context.
why: Small-page ratio rises from ~2x to 3x or more, making zswap/hardware compressed tiers 30-50% more effective at saving DRAM.

title: Magnifying glass: foveated KV precision around attention focus
idea: Like foveated rendering, the KV manager keeps recent tokens and retrieval anchors at FP8, mid-distance tokens at 3-bit and far tokens merged into learned gist tokens, re-sharpening a region from a flash copy when attention mass returns to it.
why: 4-10x KV footprint reduction on long contexts with bounded quality loss.

title: Colander: learned index models replace in-memory B-trees
idea: A colander keeps only what matters: replace database and key-value indexes with piecewise-linear learned models plus small error buffers, evaluated by a tiny controller-side unit, so index structures shrink from GBs to MBs.
why: Indexes are often 20-50% of in-memory database DRAM; 10-100x index compression.

title: Mosaic tiles: embedding tables assembled from shared tile codebooks
idea: A mosaic renders any image from a few tile colours: store recommendation embedding rows as product-quantized codes into a few shared codebooks, decoded by a memory-side gather engine on a CXL device so the host still sees full-precision rows.
why: Recsys embedding tables reach TBs and are the largest DRAM consumer in ad datacenters; 8-16x compression.

title: Post-it note: back-end oxide-TFT metadata layer stuck atop DRAM
idea: A sticky note added after the book is printed: deposit a <=350 C IGZO thin-film-transistor memory layer on top of finished DRAM or controller wafers to hold compression tags, hotness counters and dedup pointers; because metadata is recomputable it needs only seconds of retention and tolerates bit loss.
why: Frees the 3-6% of DRAM bits and the metadata-cache misses that compression/dedup cost; all added steps are back-end compatible (<=400 C) on mature US tools.

title: Crime-scene fingerprint: hybrid-bonded dedup base die under DRAM
idea: Fingerprints expose duplicates: a logic die hybrid-bonded (Cu-Cu anneal ~250-300 C) beneath a DRAM stack hashes every written line, keeps the fingerprint table in on-die SRAM and transparently stores duplicate lines once, exposing more logical than physical capacity to the host.
why: Virtualized and AI fleets show 20-40% duplicate lines; module-level dedup multiplies capacity 1.2-1.6x with assembly entirely below 400 C.

title: Stained glass from shards: salvaged DRAM dies become CXL expanders
idea: Artists turn shards into windows: desolder DRAM packages from decommissioned servers (reflow <260 C), retest and bin them, and remount them on low-temperature panel-level substrates behind a compressing CXL controller, producing new capacity-tier modules from e-waste.
why: Millions of DDR4 DIMMs retire yearly; reuse adds supply at near-zero wafer cost and no high-temperature step, and compression makes old density competitive (~2x effective).

title: Beach metal detector: back-end capacitive key-sketch array picks tokens
idea: Sweep a detector before digging: keep 1-bit sketches of all keys in a back-end HZO/MIM capacitive compute-in-memory array (crystallized <=400 C) on the accelerator; a query is broadcast as charge, the array returns top-k token indices in one shot, and only those full K/V blocks are fetched from a cheap CXL/flash tier.
why: Full KV leaves HBM entirely (10-50x less DRAM for long context) because only ~1-5% of tokens are fetched per step.

title: Reference-only reading room: back-end ReRAM layer holds model weights
idea: Reference books are read but never checked out: deposit HfOx/TaOx ReRAM crossbars (<=400 C) in the accelerator's upper metal stack to hold inference weights written once per deployment (needing only ~1e3-1e4 endurance), leaving DRAM/HBM for KV and activations only.
why: Weights are 40-70% of inference HBM; monolithic back-end storage frees that capacity while sidestepping the unlimited-endurance requirement that killed ReRAM as DRAM.

title: Jacquard punch cards: via-programmed ROM stores frozen base model
idea: A loom's pattern is punched holes: freeze a foundation model's weights into mask-ROM where one cheap via mask (no EUV, back-end only, <=400 C) programs every bit, stacked in 2-4 back-end crosspoint layers on a logic chip; fine-tunes and LoRA deltas stay in DRAM.
why: ROM is denser, refresh-free and capex-light versus DRAM; for million-unit edge/inference SKUs base-weight DRAM goes to zero.

title: Hologram sticker: photopolymer slab stores weights read by light
idea: Credit-card holograms are cheap: record model weights as page holograms in a room-temperature-cured photopolymer slab and read millions of bits per laser flash onto a CMOS image sensor beside the accelerator, streaming weights optically instead of holding them in DRAM.
why: Volume holography could hold TBs per cm^3 for a few dollars with zero high-temperature processing; weight DRAM eliminated for read-only models if readout reaches ~100 GB/s.

title: Hearing-aid retrofit: compressing buffer chips reflowed onto existing RDIMMs
idea: Retrofit rather than replace: swap the data-buffer/RCD chips on installed DDR5 RDIMMs (rework <260 C) for pin-compatible buffers that compress lines inline and advertise larger capacity through SPD, so existing DIMMs grow ~1.5x without new DRAM dies.
why: Capacity uplift on the installed base using only low-temperature assembly, deployable by US rework shops within months.

title: Melting snowman: MoS2 back-end scratchpad for transient activations
idea: A snowman only needs to last the afternoon: transfer monolayer MoS2 transistors (<=300 C) into the accelerator's back-end as 2T gain-cell scratchpads whose ultra-low leakage holds charge 1-10 s without refresh, sized for inter-layer activations that live only milliseconds.
why: Activations stop round-tripping through HBM; activation DRAM drops 2-5x and refresh disappears for that data.

title: Bucket brigade: oxide-TFT charge-transfer FIFO for pipelined activations
idea: Firefighters pass buckets down a line: build a back-end IGZO charge-transfer shift-register (CCD-like) memory that supports only FIFO access, eliminating row decoders and most sense amps, and use it for pipeline-parallel activation queues and streamed weights, which are naturally sequential.
why: Periphery is ~49% of the DRAM die (fact 7); a decoder-less FIFO memory reaches ~2x bit density and replaces DRAM for sequential buffers, all at <=400 C.

title: Velcro: detachable memory chiplets outlive their accelerators
idea: Velcro lets parts be reused: attach LPDDR/HBM-class memory to accelerators with low-temperature anisotropic conductive film or fine-pitch sockets (<200 C) instead of permanent solder and underfill, so memory is harvested and redeployed when the compute die is replaced every 2-3 years.
why: Memory lasts 8-10 years while accelerators last 2-3; reuse multiplies effective supply ~2-3x over a decade.

title: Coat check ticket: park idle chat KV with recompute receipts
idea: Hand over the coat, keep a ticket: when a chat session idles >30 s its KV is cut to 2-bit and moved to flash, keeping only a ticket (token IDs plus which layers need exact recompute); on resume the engine recomputes the quality-critical layers and dequantizes the rest. Ships as serving firmware with no fabrication step.
why: Most sessions sit idle most of the time; KV DRAM held per user drops 10-30x.

title: Seashell spiral: logarithmically spaced KV retention with merged summaries
idea: Nautilus chambers grow geometrically: keep every token of the last 256, every 2nd from 256-1k, every 4th from 1k-4k and so on, folding dropped tokens' KV into their surviving neighbour by attention-weighted averaging, so KV grows O(log n). Pure software, nothing fabricated.
why: Long-context KV becomes O(log n) instead of O(n): a 1M-token context fits in roughly 20k tokens of KV.

title: Watercolor wash: printed analog crossbar on glass computes edge weights
idea: Watercolour is painted at room temperature: solution-process perovskite or organic memristor crossbars (<150 C) on glass, program model weights as conductances and compute matrix-vector products in place for small edge models, so devices ship with no DRAM for weights.
why: Edge/IoT inference drops DRAM entirely; panel-scale low-temperature processing gives very low capex and is US-buildable.

title: Lighthouse beam: SiN photonic broadcast streams weights to accelerators
idea: One lighthouse serves many ships: a single weight memory broadcasts each layer over PECVD silicon-nitride waveguides (<=400 C) on a panel interposer to N accelerators at once using WDM, so each accelerator holds only a two-layer ring buffer instead of a full replica.
why: Replicas stop duplicating weights; weight DRAM per accelerator falls N-fold (8-32x).

title: Club sandwich: hybrid-bonded SRAM decks swallow activations
idea: Stack more layers in the sandwich: hybrid-bond (<300 C) 2-4 dense SRAM dies onto the accelerator, sized to keep a full transformer block's activations and the hottest KV pages on-package so they never spill to HBM.
why: Cuts HBM capacity needed per accelerator 20-40% and avoids TSV-heavy HBM stacks (fact 6) for working buffers.

title: Family tree: fine-tuned variants stored as 1-bit deltas
idea: Siblings share most genes: serve hundreds of fine-tuned models from one base copy plus per-variant sign-bit deltas with per-row scales, applied on the fly inside the matmul kernel. Software and firmware only, no process step.
why: Serving 100 variants needs ~1.1x base-model memory instead of 100x.

title: Sushi conveyor: CNT logic over DRAM decodes compressed KV in place
idea: Dishes pass the chef on a belt: deposit carbon-nanotube FET logic (<=325 C) on top of the DRAM array's metal stack so 2-bit compressed KV rows passing the sense amps are decoded and dot-producted with the query right there, returning only scores and selected values.
why: KV can live at 2-bit density permanently (4-8x capacity) because decompressed copies never need buffer space; also cuts data movement (fact 5).

title: Sundial: leaky back-end TFT capacitors timestamp page age
idea: A sundial tells time without gears: give each 2 MB region a back-end IGZO TFT 'age capacitor' recharged on access that leaks predictably; the controller reads its voltage to rank regions for compression or demotion, getting LRU age from physics with zero DRAM bits or counter traffic.
why: Cheap, good-enough aging lets compression/tiering pick victims well, raising off-DRAM footprint by 10-20 points; back-end only.

title: Customs declaration: pages declare tolerated error for lossy compression
idea: Goods declare their contents at the border: add 2 tolerance bits to page-table entries (exact, 1e-3, 1e-2, 1e-1 relative error) that runtimes set for activations, gradients and embeddings, letting the memory controller apply lossy codecs (mantissa truncation, block floating point) to tagged pages. OS and firmware only.
why: Approximation-tolerant data is 30-60% of AI memory; lossy encoding gives 2-4x on that share.

title: Firefly anti-sync: scheduler de-phases co-located memory peaks
idea: Fireflies synchronize; we do the opposite: the cluster scheduler profiles each job's periodic memory peaks (optimizer steps, checkpoints, GC, batch spikes) and shifts their phases so peaks on a shared pool never coincide, then sizes the pool for the sum of averages. Pure scheduling, nothing fabricated.
why: Shared-pool DRAM falls 20-35% for periodic workloads.

title: Kintsugi: OS maps around defects, accepting flawed DRAM dies
idea: Kintsugi makes broken pottery valuable: qualify DIMMs with up to ~1% failing rows, ship each module's defect map in SPD, and have firmware/OS permanently retire those pages at boot; modules are built with standard <260 C reflow only.
why: Turns yield fallout and downbinned dies into sellable capacity, plausibly +3-8% bit supply at zero fab capex.

title: Dandelion seeds: erasure-coded in-memory data replaces triple replicas
idea: Dandelions scatter many small seeds rather than three big ones: in-memory caches and stores (Redis, parameter servers, checkpoint shards) replace 3x DRAM replication with Reed-Solomon 10+4 striping across nodes, rebuilding lost shards from peers over RDMA. Software only.
why: Redundancy overhead drops from 200% to 40%, freeing ~50% of DRAM in replicated memory tiers.
